docRequirement: large-codebases.md:242 — "Sparse checkout requires git to enable `extensions.worktreeConfig` in the repository's shared `.git/config` while a sparse worktree exists. Claude Code removes that entry after the last worktree is removed, but only if Claude Code added it. It never removes a value you set yourself." So a host that uses `worktree.sparsePaths` owes three things: record whether `extensions.worktreeConfig` was already set before its first sparse-checkout, detect when the last worktree is gone, and then run the equivalent of `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig` — only on the entry it added. The page also states the failure this prevents: before v2.1.207 the leftover entry made go-git-based tools such as `tea` fail to open the repository.
current: The session worktree-lease lifecycle in server-core enables the entry and never touches it again. (1) `worktreeCreateCommands` emits `['-C', <worktreePath>, 'sparse-checkout', 'set', '--cone', ...sparsePaths]` whenever `worktree.sparsePaths` is non-empty — packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:85-89 (early-returns with no sparse command when the list is empty, :84). It is the module's only argv builder for creation and has exactly one production call site, packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10176-10185. (2) The removal handler is two lines and one command: `remove: async lease => { const root = await projectRoot(); await runGit(root, ['-C', root, 'worktree', 'remove', lease.path], 'remove') }` — packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10210-10213. No `git config` invocation exists in that closure, in worktree-git-plan.ts, or anywhere in the worktree path; `grep -ran "config', '--unset"` over packages/apps has one hit, packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/claude-bash-rule.ts:269, an `env -u` flag table in a different subsystem. (3) No ownership record and no last-worktree count: the lease record `PiWorktreeLeaseV1` (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:224-246) has no field for it, `git worktree list` is never run (only `worktree remove`, SessionManager.ts:10212), and the only other removal route — `WorktreeLeaseService.sweepOrphans` → `releaseUnlocked` → `this.options.git.remove` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:150-194, :330-336) — funnels through the same closure, so it inherits the same omission. (4) The side effect is documented and nothing acts on it: packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:38-44 ("While a sparse worktree exists git enables `extensions.worktreeConfig` in the repository's shared `.git/config`, which is a side effect on the MAIN checkout"). `grep -ran "worktreeConfig"` over packages/apps matches that comment alone. (5) Measured on git 2.43.0 with our exact argv: a scratch repo gains `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` in the shared `.git/config` at the `sparse-checkout set --cone` step (absent before both `worktree add --no-checkout` and the sparse-set), and after `git worktree remove` of the LAST worktree the entry is still `true` — git does not clean it up.
divergence: The cleanup step is entirely absent; nothing about what we do run is wrong. The key name, the value and the enabling mechanism are git's own and correct — the delta is a missing post-removal `git config --local --unset extensions.worktreeConfig`, plus the two pieces of state that gate it per the doc's carve-out: an "we added it" ownership marker taken BEFORE the first sparse-set, and a "no worktrees left" count taken AFTER the remove. Because the ownership probe has to happen before the entry exists, this cannot be retrofitted as a removal-only change. One Nessy-specific wrinkle: leases are per session under one shared per-repo namespace root (`<parent-of-repo>/.nessy-worktrees/<repo>/<leaseId>`, SessionManager.ts:10105-10110), so "last worktree" must be computed from git (`git worktree list --porcelain`), not from one `WorktreeLeaseService` instance's lease list.

change.what: Add two pure argv builders in the existing WorktreeGitCommand style. Probe (run before the first sparse-set): `{ operation: 'worktree-config-probe', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'config', '--local', '--get', 'extensions.worktreeConfig'], allowFailure: true }` — exit 1 with empty output means absent, verified on git 2.43.0. Cleanup (run after a successful remove): a list of `{ operation: 'worktree-list', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'] }` and `{ operation: 'worktree-config-unset', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'config', '--local', '--unset', 'extensions.worktreeConfig'], allowFailure: true }`. `allowFailure: true` on the unset is load-bearing: `git config --unset` of an absent key exits 5 (measured), and runWorktreeGit throws `worktree-git-<op>-failed` on any non-zero without it. Use `--local` explicitly on both read and write so a value in the user's global config is never read as ours and never unset. Keep the module doc comment's habit of naming the reason.

Claim ownership before the sparse-set. When `settings.sparsePaths.length > 0`, run the probe once against `root` before iterating `worktreeCreateCommands`; if the key is absent (non-zero exit or empty trimmed output), create an idempotent marker file at `join((await worktreeAuthority()).namespaceRoot, '.worktree-config-owned')` (that directory is already mkdir'd at 10110 and is already an additionalWritableRoot at 10131). Write with flag `'wx'` and swallow EEXIST so a second concurrent session does not fail creation. If the probe says the key is already set, do NOT write the marker — that is the doc's "never removes a value you set yourself". The marker belongs here rather than on the lease record because it is per-repository and must outlive every session; putting it on `PiWorktreeLeaseV1` (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:224) would both scope it wrongly and change persisted session state.

After the existing `worktree remove` succeeds, add the cleanup: if the marker file exists, run `worktree list --porcelain` against `root` and count lines starting with `worktree ` — exactly 1 means the main checkout only, no linked worktrees left (measured: 2 with one linked worktree, 1 with none). Only then run the `--local --unset`, and on success unlink the marker. Wrap the whole cleanup in try/catch that logs via `sessionLog.warn` and swallows: a failed cosmetic cleanup must not surface as `worktree-remove-failed`, which is what `releaseUnlocked` turns a throw from this closure into (worktree-lease-service.ts:330-334) and which would leave a residual and block workspace drain. Guard: skip the unset when a per-worktree config file exists at `<sharedGitDir>/config.worktree`, since unsetting the extension would make git stop reading it.

change.symbol: new describe beside 'worktree.sparsePaths reaches worktree creation' (:32)
change.what: Assert the two new argv lists exactly, including `--local`, the key spelling `extensions.worktreeConfig`, and `allowFailure: true` on probe and unset. The existing create-path assertions (:64-67) are unchanged because the probe is issued by the caller, not appended to `worktreeCreateCommands`.

Deliberately keep the `git` port shape `create/inspect/remove` (worktree-lease-service.ts:90-94). Adding a member would break the seven `git: { … }` stubs across worktree-lease-service.test.ts (:20, :121, :149, :162, :179, :194) and worktree-orphan-sweep.test.ts (:46) for no gain — all cleanup lives inside the closures SessionManager already owns.

blastRadius: Confined to the worktree lifecycle in packages/server-core, no wire or schema change if the marker-file design is used. Readers: `createPiWorktreeLeaseService` is the single construction site of `WorktreeLeaseService` (11 call sites in SessionManager.ts) and both its closures are called from `recoverUnlocked`, `releaseUnlocked` and `sweepOrphansUnlocked` (worktree-lease-service.ts:290-311, :317-337, :150-194), so the orphan sweep (SessionManager.ts:10064, :10758) inherits the cleanup for free. Tests touched: worktree-git-plan.test.ts only; the lease-service and orphan-sweep suites stay green because the port shape does not change. Sandbox: the unset runs through `runWorktreeGit` (SessionManager.ts:10020-10048) with `profile: 'read-only'` and `additionalWritableRoots: [root, namespaceRoot]`; `<root>/.git/config` sits inside `root` and is in no deny floor — `selfConfigDenyWriteRoots` denies only `.claude`/`.nessy-agent`/`.agents` and user-scope config (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/isolation/self-config-deny.ts:59-73), and `sharedGitDirectoryGrant` (whose `deniedWriteRoots` DO include `config`) resolves to undefined here because the spawn's workspaceRoot is the containment root, not a linked worktree (isolation.ts:279-283). So no isolation change is needed — but if the project root is itself a linked worktree the shared `.git` lies outside every writable root, and the unset will be denied; `allowFailure` plus the swallow keeps that harmless. Explicit risk boundaries: (a) the change WRITES to the user's own repository `.git/config`, i.e. state Nessy does not own and cannot recreate — that is why the ownership probe, the count and the `config.worktree` guard are all preconditions, not niceties; (b) the marker file is new on-disk state under `<parent-of-repo>/.nessy-worktrees/<repo>/`, a filesystem persistence boundary shared across sessions and concurrent processes, so it must be created idempotently and removed only under the same gate; (c) if a future revision instead records ownership on `PiWorktreeLeaseV1` / `PiWorktreeLeaseStateV1` (packages/shared/src/sessions/types.ts:224-251) it crosses the persisted session-state boundary and becomes a schema risk trigger.
userImpact: None observable for a default install: `worktree.sparsePaths` defaults to `[]` (WORKTREE_SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:71-76) and `worktreeCreateCommands` emits no sparse command for an empty list (worktree-git-plan.ts:84), so no sparse-checkout ever runs and the entry is never enabled. It surfaces the moment a user puts `worktree.sparsePaths` in `~/.nessy-agent/config.json` (read live per operation, SessionManager.ts:10116 via getUserWorktreeSettings, packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:1313) and then uses a worktree — `EnterWorktree`, or a subagent worktree lease. From then on, permanently and silently: their main checkout carries `[extensions] worktreeConfig = true` in `.git/config` after every Nessy worktree is gone, and go-git-based tools — the page names `tea` — refuse to open the repository until the user runs `git config --unset extensions.worktreeConfig` by hand. Nothing in Nessy's UI mentions the entry or the fix, and the repository the user is left holding is their own.
notes: Every file cited was read in full at the quoted lines (worktree-git-plan.ts, worktree-lease-service.ts, SessionManager.ts 10020-10221, worktree-settings.ts, types.ts 224-251, isolation.ts 255-372, isolation/self-config-deny.ts, isolation/shared-git.ts, storage.ts 1305-1323, worktree-git-plan.test.ts, the two lease-service suites' git stubs). git behaviour was re-measured here, not inherited from the verdict: on git 2.43.0 our exact argv enables the entry, `worktree remove` of the last worktree leaves it, `config --local --get` of an absent key exits 1, `config --unset` of an absent key exits 5, and `worktree list --porcelain` prints one `worktree ` line with no linked worktrees. Two things I could not verify. (1) The `config.worktree` edge: no such file was created in an ordinary repo in my repro, so the claim that unsetting the extension could orphan a migrated `core.bare`/`core.worktree` is reasoning about git's documented migration, not a measurement — hence it is phrased as a guard. (2) The doc does not say HOW Claude Code records its ownership, so the marker-file mechanism is our design choice, not a matched implementation detail; any equivalent record satisfies the sentence. Adjacent but NOT this finding, so filed nowhere here: `getUserWorktreeSettings` reads only the user `config.json` layer, while the page describes these keys living in `.claude/settings.json` — a separate scope divergence on the same page. Also checked and rejected as the classic wrong subsystem: the `sparsePaths` in packages/shared/src/plugins/store.ts:55 and marketplace/registry-source.ts:268 is the plugin-registry field, explicitly not git sparse-checkout (registry-catalog-fetcher.ts:289-290), and it never runs git.
